interest: This file provides a fascinating snapshot of Japanese youth internationalism and pacifist sentiment in late 1932, coming just over a year after the Mukden Incident and amidst Japan's deepening diplomatic isolation. The Boy Scouts' message demonstrates how Western-originated civic organizations and the memory of the 1918 Armistice retained cultural and moral resonance among Japanese youth. Furthermore, Ambassador Grew's dispatch reveals his keen interest in identifying counterweights to rising insular nationalism, finding significance in ordinary civic gestures that affirmed a shared global identity.
overview: This file comprises records concerning an Armistice Day goodwill visit made by Japanese Boy Scouts to the American Embassy in Tokyo in November 1932. In Despatch No. 191, dated November 12, 1932, U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew informs the Secretary of State that a delegation of fourteen Tokyo Boy Scouts visited the Embassy and presented a short peace address. Grew transmits the enclosed text at their request, observing that the gesture reflects a desire among Japanese youth to participate in global peace and see themselves as part of the wider international community rather than remaining insular. The file includes a State Department Document File cross-reference sheet (894.4081/1 referencing 894.415/2), Grew's two-page diplomatic despatch, and the text of the address signed by Kiyota Hashimoto of the Seinan Boy Scouts.

subfiles.about: A State Department document file note cross-referencing Despatch No. 191 concerning an address presented by Tokyo Boy Scouts.
subfiles.summary: This State Department document file note indexes Despatch No. 191 dated November 12, 1932, from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Japan. It directs the reader to decimal file 894.415/2 for the original dispatch. The note records that the despatch transmits a copy of an address presented to the Embassy on Armistice Day by the Tokyo Boy Scouts.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Despatch No. 191 regarding Tokyo Boy Scouts

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reporting on an Armistice Day visit to the American Embassy by a delegation of Tokyo Boy Scouts.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew informs the Secretary of State that a group of fourteen young Boy Scouts representing the scouts of Tokyo visited the American Embassy on Armistice Day. They presented a short address promoting peace and goodwill, which Grew encloses at their request. Grew remarks that while the incident was minor, it signaled that Japanese youth were not entirely self-centered and desired to be part of the global community.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 191 from Joseph C. Grew to the Secretary of State regarding Address presented by Japanese Boy Scouts

subfiles.about: An address delivered by the Seinan Boy Scouts to the American Embassy conveying Armistice Day peace greetings and goodwill to American youth.
subfiles.summary: Signed by Kiyota Hashimoto on behalf of the Seinan Boy Scouts, this address expresses the scouts' desire to contribute to preserving world peace achieved after the 1918 Armistice. The scouts affirm their fellowship with youth of all nations and races in Japan and worldwide. They extend sincere goodwill to the youth of the United States via the American Embassy.
subfiles.title: Address presented by the Seinan Boy Scouts on Armistice Day
